questions.stem: What does the boy take with him when he sets out?

options.C: a rifle and a black dog
options.D: a bag of food and a map

questions.explanation: The poem opens with the blacksmith's boy going out with a rifle and his black dog running behind.

questions.stem: Cobwebs, rivers and thorn branches try to stop the boy. How does the poet make nature seem?

options.C: as if it is alive and deliberately trying to block him

questions.explanation: Nature is personified: things 'snatch', 'hinder' and 'catch' at him as if they want to stop him.

distractors.D: they try to stop and even blind him

questions.stem: When things go wrong, the boy keeps saying what he can do (break branches, swim rivers, stare out spiders). What does this show?

options.A: He is lying to his dog.
options.B: He is brave and determined, and talks himself through his fears.

questions.explanation: His boasts keep his courage up as each danger appears: he won't let the obstacles beat him.

questions.stem: The boy ends up carrying the rainbow 'instead of his broken gun'. What could this suggest?

options.A: He sold his gun to buy a rainbow.
options.B: His courage is rewarded with something beautiful and magical, not won by force.
options.C: He has learned to make rainbows.
options.D: The rainbow is a new kind of weapon.

questions.explanation: His gun breaks, yet he wins the rainbow: a gentle, magical prize that suits a legend more than a weapon does.

distractors.C: he catches it; he doesn't make it
distractors.D: it's a prize, not a weapon

options.A: It tells a story like an old folk tale, with magic and a hero.
options.B: It is a set of instructions.
options.C: It describes a real person from history.
options.D: It is a true story from the newspaper.

questions.explanation: A legend is a traditional story with heroes and wonders. The boy's journey, the talking crow, and catching a rainbow belong to that kind of tale.

distractors.C: the boy is a story character

questions.stem: By the end, the whole world says nobody is braver or bolder than the boy. What is the mood of the ending?
questions.explanation: After all the dangers, he comes home with the rainbow on his shoulder and everyone praises him: the ending celebrates his victory.

passages.title: Legend – Judith Wright
passages.intro: Find and read this poem before you start.
passages.credit: The poem is still in copyright, so it is not printed here.
paragraphs: Read 'Legend' by Judith Wright. It is in Judith Wright's 'Collected Poems' and in many school anthologies; you can also find it by searching the title and poet online.
The poem tells, like an old folk tale, the story of a blacksmith's boy who sets out on a journey.
Keep the poem open next to this app while you answer. Read it twice: once for the story, once for how it is written.
